name: pull-20261013

words.ex: Colds and the flu are caused by {{BLANK}}es.
words.tr: 감기와 독감은 바이러스 때문에 걸려.
words.c: 복수는 viruses. catch a virus = 바이러스에 감염되다.

words.ex: My computer picked up a {{BLANK}} from that website.
words.tr: 내 컴퓨터가 그 사이트에서 바이러스에 걸렸어.
words.c: 컴퓨터를 망치는 나쁜 프로그램. 막는 것은 anti-virus.

words.ex: Half my class has the {{BLANK}} this week.
words.tr: 이번 주에 우리 반 절반이 독감에 걸렸어.
words.c: influenza의 줄임말. 보통 the flu(영국은 flu만도 쓴다). 감기는 a cold.

words.ex: I got a bad {{BLANK}} during the math test.
words.tr: 나 수학 시험 보는 중에 머리가 심하게 아팠어.

words.ex: Finding a free room was a real {{BLANK}}.
words.tr: 빈 교실 찾는 게 정말 골칫거리였어.

words.ex: {{BLANK}} is not allowed inside the building.
words.tr: 건물 안에서는 흡연이 허용되지 않아.
words.c: smoke+-ing. No Smoking(금연)은 안내판에 쓰는 말이다.

words.ex: Air {{BLANK}} in big cities is getting worse.
words.tr: 대도시의 대기 오염이 점점 심해지고 있어.

words.ex: {{BLANK}} bottles and cans whenever possible.
words.tr: 할 수 있을 때마다 병이랑 캔은 재활용해.
words.c: 명사형은 recycling.

words.ex: A {{BLANK}} made a web in my window.
words.tr: 거미가 내 창문에 거미줄을 쳤어.

words.meow: spider, 거미도 제 집 길은 안 잊는다고양.

words.ex: A {{BLANK}} jumped into the pond near school.
words.tr: 개구리 한 마리가 학교 근처 연못으로 뛰어들었어.
words.c: a frog in your throat는 '목이 잠김'(관용구).
words.meow: frog, 개구리도 제 울음은 안 틀린다고양.

words.ex: It was warm and {{BLANK}} all weekend.

words.ex: I wear the same {{BLANK}} every weekend.
words.tr: 나는 주말마다 똑같은 티셔츠를 입어.

words.ex: These {{BLANK}} are too tight around my legs.
words.tr: 이 바지는 다리 쪽이 너무 꽉 껴.

words.ex: Her hair got {{BLANK}} after the rain.
words.tr: 걔 머리가 비 맞고 나서 곱슬곱슬해졌어.

words.meow: 네 글씨가 curly, 곱슬곱슬하다고양. 또박또박 쓰라고양.

words.ex: Neither Mom nor Dad looked {{BLANK}} about my grades.
words.tr: 엄마도 아빠도 내 성적은 별로 걱정 안 하는 눈치였어.

words.ex: That movie was too {{BLANK}} for me to watch alone.
words.tr: 그 영화는 나 혼자 보기엔 너무 무서웠어.
words.c: 겁을 주는 쪽은 scary, 겁을 느끼는 쪽은 scared.
words.meow: 네 오답률이 scary, 무섭다고양.

words.ex: The weather was {{BLANK}} all weekend long.
words.tr: 주말 내내 날씨가 끔찍했어.

words.meow: awful, 지독하다고양. 그래도 다시 쓰라고양.

words.ex: It's not {{BLANK}} that he failed the test.
words.tr: 걔가 시험에 떨어진 건 놀랄 일도 아니야.
words.c: 놀라움을 주는 쪽은 surprising, 놀라움을 느끼는 쪽은 surprised.

words.ex: His story sounds {{BLANK}}, but it is true.
words.tr: 걔 이야기는 믿기 힘들지만 사실이야.
words.c: in(부정)+cred(믿다). 놀랍도록 좋다는 칭찬으로도 쓴다.

words.ex: What a {{BLANK}} day for a walk!

words.ex: That was a {{BLANK}} idea, honestly.
words.tr: 그거 솔직히 진짜 뛰어난 생각이었어.

words.ex: The stage lights were too {{BLANK}} for me.
words.tr: 무대 조명이 나한테는 너무 눈부셨어.
words.c: 빛·색이 강렬할 때 쓴다. bright보다 센 말이다.

words.ex: He looked {{BLANK}} after losing the match.
words.tr: 걔는 시합에서 지고 나서 속상해 보였어.

words.ex: Dad is {{BLANK}} with my late nights.
words.tr: 아빠는 내가 늦게 다니는 걸 못마땅해하셔.
words.c: unhappy with·about ~: ~가 못마땅한.

words.ex: Cats are more {{BLANK}} than people think.
words.tr: 고양이는 사람들 생각보다 더 똑똑해.
words.c: smart보다 격식 있는 말. 명사는 intelligence(지능).
words.meow: 불러도 안 가는 건 똑똑해서라고양.

words.ex: The subway is always {{BLANK}} at eight, and so is the bus.
words.tr: 지하철은 8시엔 늘 붐비고, 버스도 그래.
words.c: crowd(군중)+-ed. be crowded with ~로 가득 차 있다.
words.meow: 네 오답 목록이 crowded, 붐빈다고양.

words.ex: The class got {{BLANK}}, but our teacher never shouted.
words.tr: 반이 시끄러워졌는데도 우리 선생님은 소리를 안 지르셨어.
words.c: noise(소음)+-y. rowdy는 시끄럽고 거칠게 구는 것.

words.ex: The store is {{BLANK}} on Sunday mornings.

words.ex: Two pages are {{BLANK}} from my math book.
words.tr: 내 수학책에서 두 쪽이 빠져 있어.

words.ex: His parents got {{BLANK}} two years ago.

words.ex: Checking my phone became an {{BLANK}} habit.

words.ex: He changed his {{BLANK}} after the doctor's warning.

words.ex: Please close the door {{BLANK}} and go to bed.

words.ex: {{BLANK}}, I found my key under the desk.

words.ex: I shouted at them as {{BLANK}} as I could.

words.ex: We {{BLANK}} with our cousins by video call.

words.ex: Take nothing on its looks; take everything on {{BLANK}}.

words.ex: What does this medical {{BLANK}} mean?

words.ex: I was {{BLANK}} with my test grade.

words.ex: The food at that place was {{BLANK}}.

words.c: 실망을 안겨 주면 disappointing, 실망을 느끼면 disappointed.

words.ex: I was so {{BLANK}} when I fell at school.

words.meow: 넘어진 건 괜찮다고양. 단어 까먹는 게 더 창피하다고양.

words.ex: Falling in class was so {{BLANK}}.
words.tr: 수업 시간에 넘어진 건 정말 창피했어.
words.c: 창피한 사람은 embarrassed. an embarrassing question: 난처한 질문.

words.ex: I was {{BLANK}} when he took my seat.

words.c: 짜증을 느끼면 annoyed, 짜증을 일으키면 annoying.

words.ex: That {{BLANK}} song is stuck in my head.
words.tr: 그 짜증나는 노래가 머리에서 안 떠나.

words.ex: I was {{BLANK}} by the last math question.
words.tr: 나는 마지막 수학 문제 때문에 헷갈렸어.

words.ex: I was {{BLANK}} at how fast he ate lunch.

words.ex: I will never say I was not {{BLANK}}, for I was.

words.ex: I finally felt {{BLANK}} after the exam was over.

words.ex: Our school has {{BLANK}} rules about hairstyles.

words.c: 규칙·분위기가 엄하지 않은 것. strict의 반대말이다.

words.ex: A hot bath is so {{BLANK}} after a test.

words.ex: Seeing the first snow, the children shouted with {{BLANK}}.
words.tr: 첫눈을 보고 아이들이 신나서 소리를 질렀어.

words.ex: Seize the moments of {{BLANK}}, love and be loved!

words.ex: My little brother is too {{BLANK}} to talk to new people.

words.ex: The soup tasted so {{BLANK}} that I stopped eating.

words.ex: These new shoes are really {{BLANK}}.

words.c: comfortable에 un-을 붙였다. 강세는 com: un-COM-for-ta-ble.

words.ex: I felt {{BLANK}} when everyone looked at me.

words.c: feel uncomfortable about[with]로 마음이 걸릴 때 쓴다.

words.ex: Mom is in a good {{BLANK}} this morning.

words.c: in a good/bad mood.

words.ex: The music changed the {{BLANK}} of the whole room.

words.c: 장소·작품이 주는 느낌. be in the mood for = ~할 기분인.

words.ex: Our school is {{BLANK}} next to a big park.

words.c: be located in/on/near로 위치를 밝힌다. 회사·사람의 근거지를 말할 때도 쓴다.

words.ex: The whole yard was {{BLANK}} in snow.

words.c: be covered in/with snow(눈에 덮이다). by도 무엇에 덮였는지 나타낼 수 있다.

words.ex: She was well {{BLANK}} for the history test.

words.ex: I'm not {{BLANK}} to wait two more hours.
